description: Vary the auxiliary-field term $-|F|^{2}=-\bar{F}F$ using the given $�\delta_{\eta}F$ and $�\delta_{\eta}\bar{F}$, and combine it with the $F$-dependent part of the fermion kinetic variation from Step 3 to verify that these terms cancel for the same value of $a$ found in Step 4.
reasoning: The auxiliary term only depends on $F$ and $\bar F$, so its variation is directly $-(\delta\bar F)F-\bar F\delta F$. Substituting the given SUSY variations gives two terms: one proportional to $F\partial\bar\xi\bar\sigma\eta$ and one proportional to $\bar F\bar\eta\bar\sigma\partial\xi$. The fermion kinetic term contains corresponding $F$-dependent pieces because $\delta\xi$ has a $\sqrt2\eta F$ term and $\delta\bar\xi$ has a $\sqrt2\bar\eta\bar F$ term. The $\bar F$ term cancels locally against the second auxiliary variation. The $F$ term first appears as $\bar\xi\bar\sigma\eta\partial F$ and cancels the first auxiliary variation after integrating by parts in the action. Since $\eta$ is spacetime independent and $F$ is bosonic, no extra sign arises in the integration by parts beyond the usual minus sign. The cancellation is independent of the scalar-variation coefficient $a$, so it remains valid for the Step 4 value $a=-\sqrt2$.
result:
The auxiliary-field contribution is
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F=\delta_\eta(-\bar F F)=-(\delta_\eta\bar F)F-\bar F(\delta_\eta F).
$$
Using
$$
\delta_\eta F=i\sqrt2\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi,
\qquad
\delta_\eta\bar F=-i\sqrt2\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta,
$$
one obtains
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F
= i\sqrt2\,F\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta
-i\sqrt2\,\bar F\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi.}
$$
Now isolate the $F$-dependent part of the fermion kinetic variation
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi=i\delta\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi+i\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu(\delta\xi).
$$
From
$$
\delta\bar\xi\big|_{\bar F}=\sqrt2\bar\eta\bar F,
\qquad
\delta\xi\big|_F=\sqrt2\eta F,
$$
we get
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_F
=i\sqrt2\,\bar F\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi
+i\sqrt2\,\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta\,\partial_\mu F.
$$
In the action, integrate the second term by parts, with $\eta$ constant:
$$
\int d^4x\,i\sqrt2\,\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta\,\partial_\mu F
\doteq
-\int d^4x\,i\sqrt2\,F\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta,
$$
where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to a total derivative. Hence
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_F
\doteq
 i\sqrt2\,\bar F\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi
-i\sqrt2\,F\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta.}
$$
Adding this to $\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F$ gives
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F+\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_F\doteq 0.
$$
Thus the $F$-dependent terms cancel off shell, modulo a total derivative. This cancellation does not introduce any new condition on $a$; it is therefore consistent with the value already fixed in Step 4, namely
$$
a=a^*=-\sqrt2.
$$
